 - [Voice tools](../../../../docs/gitbooks/en/features/native-tools/voice.md)
 - [tinyvoice submodule](../../../../vendor/tinyvoice/README.md)
 - [Chat](../../../../docs/gitbooks/en/features/chat.md)
+
+## Speech request privacy
+
+Hosted transcription, hosted reply speech and external STT/TTS calls enforce
+OpenHuman's live egress policy before dispatching HTTP requests. In local-only
+mode those cloud/provider routes fail without uploading audio or text. Dictation
+has no local STT fallback; local Piper TTS does not cross this boundary.
+Standard and sensitive modes retain the existing request and response behavior.
+
+Permitted requests emit `ExternalTransferPending` with inference as the reason,
+`FileContent` for transcription audio and `Prompt` for text sent for synthesis.
+The descriptor names the provider and destination origin only; it never includes
+URL credentials, paths, query parameters, filenames, audio or spoken text.
+Voice calls currently have no chat routing argument, so these events are
+unrouted, like other background egress events. Realtime voice sessions are a
+separate transport and are outside this change.
+
+Regression tests in [`egress_tests.rs`](./egress_tests.rs) exercise hosted STT/TTS,
+OpenAI-compatible STT/TTS, Deepgram STT and ElevenLabs STT/TTS against loopback
+mock servers, with the `voice` Cargo feature enabled.

read docs/gitbooks/en/features/privacy-m.text:
1| ---
    2| description: >-
    3|   One switch, enforced in the Rust core. Local-only mode blocks cloud model
    4|   calls, network tools, web search, integrations and cloud embeddings, and
    5|   allows only on-device runtimes. Voice is the exception, because there is no
    6|   local speech-to-text engine.
    7| icon: lock
    8| ---
    9| 
   10| # Privacy mode
   11| 
   12| Most assistants' privacy story is a paragraph in a system prompt. OpenHuman's is an enforcement point in the Rust core.
   13| 
   14| The `[privacy]` config block defines three modes:
   15| 
   16| | Mode | What it means |
   17| | --- | --- |
   18| | `standard` (default) | Normal operation. Managed cloud routing, BYO providers and local models are all available. |
   19| | `local_only` | No inference leaves the device. Every external chat provider is refused when it is built: the managed cloud, BYO cloud keys, even CLI delegates like Claude Code. Network tools, web search, integrations and cloud embeddings are refused at their egress points. Only local runtimes pass: Ollama, LM Studio, MLX and local OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Voice is the one exception, because no local speech-to-text engine exists. |
   20| | `sensitive` | The base for an upcoming PII-aware tier (detection, redaction, destination disclosure). Today it behaves like `standard`. |
   21| 
   22| ## Why enforcement matters
   23| 
   24| Privacy mode is not a policy the model is asked to follow. The first check lives in the inference provider factory (`crates/openhuman-core/src/inference/provider/factory/`). Under `local_only`, the core refuses to build an external provider at all. The error names the blocked provider and tells you how to fix it: switch to a local model, or change the mode in Settings.
   25| 
   26| That makes the guarantee independent of prompts, agents, tools or upstream bugs. If any code path tries to reach a cloud model in local-only mode, it cannot get a client.
